displayOrder.name: Precision Studio
displayOrder.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing.
Direction name: Precision Studio. Create one independent 1440 x 1024 desktop application mockup for BOX3D, an aspirational browser engineering simulation workbench. This is an active simulation application, not a landing page.
Reference image 1 is the actual current canopy workbench: preserve its purpose and core tasks, but redesign its cramped layout and abstract scene completely. Reference image 2 is an earlier industrial-test mockup: use only its credible physical materials and scene ambition, never its calibration claims or physical measurements.
Hero use case: a four-corner fabric canopy load experiment in a photoreal, sunlit industrial structural testing hall. The viewport occupies about 65 percent of the application width, is beautifully composed at an elevated three-quarter angle, and shows the entire pale ivory woven tensile membrane supported at all four corners by steel clevises, cable tensioners, grounded bolted base plates and powder-coated steel posts. Fine cloth weave, stitched reinforced edges, realistic smooth sag, stainless fixtures, subtle brushed machining marks, floor expansion joints, diffuse skylights, strong contact shadows, natural daylight, visually plausible member sizes. No people. The live-simulation scene must have genuine modeled depth and readable assembly; no neon, galaxy sky, checkerboard cloth, floating parts, luminous poles, cartoon blocks, or excessive haze.
UI: precision graphite and warm off-white typography with restrained safety-orange action color, built-in Inter and IBM Plex Mono typography, body labels 14-16px. Slim top bar reads 'BOX3D' and 'Engineering Studio', accessible primary navigation 'Experiments', 'Compare', 'Evidence'. A clear project breadcrumb 'Membrane studies / Canopy load'. Top-right single orange 'Run simulation' primary action. Small honest 'Reduced model' badge and 'PBD cloth' solver metadata. Left 216px explorer grouped into 'Specimen', 'Supports', 'Loads', 'Response'; legible selected rows with simple icons and no nested cards. Right 258px inspector only 'Load case', target '0.80 normalized', a load-mode dropdown, and compact material details 'Woven membrane'. One concise disclosure 'Comparative simulation · not calibrated' in the status line. Avoid physical kN, mm, MPa, certified, FEM, safety-pass, or calibrated claims.
Viewport has a compact 'Material / Response' segmented mode control, orbit icon and fit-view control, two small white response markers with fine leaders anchored to the fabric. At bottom one clean timeline and a single wide 'Response history' line chart with teal line, readable labels 'Model time' and 'Normalized response'; no fake physical sensor claims. All major content fits naturally in frame with no truncation. High craft, functional engineering software, beautiful enough to be a dream tool, orderly and spacious.
Do not put the entire app in a card, do not use nested cards, do not add gratuitous dashboards, metric tiles, disabled icon rows, made-up features, device bezel, browser chrome, or promotional copy. Output exactly one finished design, no collage.

displayOrder.name: Research Atelier
displayOrder.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing.
Direction name: Research Atelier. Output one independent 1440 x 1024 desktop mockup for the existing BOX3D engineering simulation application. It must be a fully designed software screen, not a marketing page.
Attached image 1 shows the current live workbench; redesign its over-dense hierarchy. Attached image 2 is an earlier industrial test concept and gives the desired physical credibility of the scene; disregard its unverified physical-unit measurements and calibration claims.
Explore a meaningfully different LIGHT product direction: warm porcelain-white panels, deep graphite text, fine cool-grey separators, subtle teal scientific annotation, restrained orange primary action. Inter for readable UI, IBM Plex Mono only for data. Generous purposeful space, 14-16px labels, polished professional desktop software. Thin top bar 'BOX3D' / 'Engineering Studio'. Navigation 'Design', 'Simulate', 'Compare'. Orange primary 'Run simulation'. Persistent project title 'Plate forming study' with muted 'Reduced material model'.
Hero: an extraordinarily realistic materials laboratory simulation viewport occupying the upper 70 percent of the central work area, not a static marketing photograph. A real-looking hydraulic load frame pressing a brushed aluminum plate over a steel support fixture. Visible grounded black machine base, machined mounting slots, four substantial cylindrical guide columns, bolts with washers, a polished ram and circular punch in contact with a gently dented metallic sheet, a clean load path and believable clearances. Sharp foreground machining detail with a softly lit neutral laboratory hall in the background, natural window illumination and fine contact shadows. Perspective angle sufficient to see plate thickness, supports and punch contact. No operators or people, neon, stars, glowing machine parts, arbitrary abstract blocks, fake bright simulation rainbows. A discreet optional 'Response overlay' toggle, default off, communicates this is interactive 3D.
Distinct layout: left a compact 200px experiment outline with an image thumbnail for this specimen and five well-spaced rows 'Geometry', 'Material', 'Supports', 'Load case', 'Results'. Main viewport is the hero with a slim lower toolstrip: orbit, fit, capture. On the right a quiet 256px 'Load case' inspector with target '0.80 normalized', 'Quasi-static sequence' as a presentation label only if needed (prefer simply 'Actuator load'), material preset 'Metal lattice', and concise 'Model assumptions' accordion. No simulated physical kN, mm, MPa, calibrated, certified, FEM, or converged claims.
Below viewport and inspector, one horizontal analysis tray with a clean line chart titled 'Load / response', labeled 'Normalized load' and 'Simulation response', plus a short run history list. Display a small unambiguous footer 'Comparative model · not calibrated'. One clear primary action, no cards-inside-cards, no random feature tiles, no dense telemetry wall, no disabled tool clutter. All content naturally fits inside 1440 x 1024 with legible labels and aligned baselines.
The result should feel like an extraordinarily well-made engineering instrument: calm, precise, intelligible, tactile physical realism, and useful for repeated experiments. Output one finished design only, no collage, no device bezel or browser chrome.

displayOrder.name: Field Observatory
displayOrder.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing.
Direction name: Field Observatory. Create one independent 1440 x 1024 desktop application mockup for BOX3D Engineering Studio, a dream workbench for engineering simulations. This is an operational simulation screen, never a landing page.
The attached screenshot is the CURRENT app and is grounding for existing experiments, controllable loads, playback, derived telemetry and reduced-model provenance. Transform its cramped tables, neon fixtures and star-field rendering into a radically clearer, scene-first engineering experience.
Hero use case: 'Suspension cable study' from the existing rope and rigging catalog. The central live 3D simulation is a magnificent photoreal architectural-scale suspension footbridge in a believable temperate river valley: two properly proportioned steel towers anchored into concrete plinths, continuous catenary main cables seated over the tower saddles, evenly spaced vertical hangers connected to the deck, a pedestrian-scale deck with edge railings and coherent abutments. Real metal junctions and bolted anchor plates visible on the nearest tower, subtly weathered structural steel, restrained warm gray concrete, natural river reflections and actual modeled ground contact. Broad daylight with pale blue sky, no stars or fantasy lighting. River bank vegetation recedes quietly so the force-carrying geometry remains readable. Nothing floats, no impossible cable connections, neon struts, cartoon cubes, or decorative sci-fi scaffolding. Treat this as a rendered physical study, do not imply the reduced rope solver models full real bridge behavior.
Distinct layout: almost full-width central scene taking 75 percent of the screen area, edge-to-edge beneath a slim warm charcoal application command bar. Small fixed 68px icon rail to the left with clear tooltips/labels 'Labs', 'Setup', 'Results'. A compact, floating flat left study outline only 224px wide, titled 'Suspension cable study', with three readable rows 'Cables', 'Supports', 'Load'. A restrained 280px inspector drawer on the right titled 'Cable response', containing current preset, 'Impulse load', magnitude '0.80 normalized', and the clear orange primary button 'Run simulation'. Controls are sparse and genuinely readable at 14-16px, Inter plus IBM Plex Mono data, warm charcoal UI, off-white text, muted amber accents, teal response traces. No nested cards.
Use one small elegant sensor callout with thin leader pointing precisely at a hanger attachment, text 'P1 · Derived response'. A compact top-center mode switch 'Material / Response'. A sophisticated single bottom analysis dock shows time scrubber with run / pause / reset and one broad graph 'Response over model time', labels 'Model time' and 'Normalized response'. Footer text 'PBD rope · comparative model · not calibrated'. Keep other views discoverable via top navigation 'Experiments', 'Compare', 'Evidence' without panels or feature inventory for each.
No physical kN, mm, MPa, certified, converged, calibrated claims. No 'AI optimization' buttons or capabilities the current code does not support. No marketing headings, statistics cards, fabricated safety results, browser chrome, device frame, collages, excessive UI glow or clipping. Output one beautifully finished, independently conceived software design.

truthBoundary: Generated concept images. Their scenes, measurements, interface controls and chart values do not establish implemented behavior, physical accuracy or completed rendering fidelity.
